title: Understanding Cross-Modal Inconsistency through Representation Subspaces in Omni Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.22619v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Omni Models process audio, vision, and text within a unified language backbone, yet often produce different answers for semantically equivalent inputs across modalities. Existing representation-level analyses do not distinguish between information that predicts whether disagreement will occur and the representation whose perturbation affects the model's answer. In this paper, we estimate a low-dimensional Answer Subspace from answer-position representations and use it to separate answer-related components from the remaining representation. Across three Omni Models and two multimodal reasoning tasks, information predictive of cross-modal inconsistency lies mainly outside the Answer Subspace, concentrating in a reproducible two-dimensional representation that is not explained by a fixed modality offset. translated_title: 通过全模态模型中的表示子空间理解跨模态不一致性
translated_abstract: 全模态模型（Omni Models）在统一的语言主干中处理音频、视觉和文本，但对于语义等价的跨模态输入，它们常常给出不同的答案。现有的表示层面分析没有区分“预测是否会发生分歧的信息”与“其扰动会影响模型答案的表示”。在本文中，我们从答案位置的表示中估计出一个低维的“答案子空间”，并利用它将答案相关成分与表示中的其余部分分离开来。在三个全模态模型和两个多模态推理任务上，预测跨模态不一致性的信息主要位于答案子空间之外，集中在一个可复现的二维表示中，且该表示无法由固定的模态偏移所解释。匹配干预实验揭示了二者不同的行为角色：扰动答案子空间会显著改变模型的预测，而……
tldr: 本文提出从答案位置表示中估计低维“答案子空间”，发现预测全模态模型跨模态不一致性的信息主要集中于答案子空间之外的一个可复现二维表示中，且该表示与答案子空间在干预下表现出截然不同的行为作用。
en_tdlr: This paper estimates a low-dimensional Answer Subspace from answer-position representations in Omni Models and shows that information predictive of cross-modal inconsistency lies mainly outside it, concentrating in a reproducible two-dimensional representation whose perturbation plays a distinct behavioral role from the Answer Subspace.
